sections.overview: Neopetalia punctata is a dragonfly in the distinctive South American family Neopetaliidae.
sections.identification: It is the sole living representative of its family; its larva helped clarify that it is not an aeshnoid dragonfly.
sections.habitat: Published accounts associate it with temperate streams in Chile and Argentina.
sections.diet: The references consulted do not provide a species-specific account of its prey.
sections.behavior: Its aquatic larva was described in a taxonomic study, but the sources consulted give little detail on adult behavior.
sections.reproduction: The larval stage is known, while detailed observations of egg-laying and development were not found in the references consulted.
sections.ecology: This relict lineage is associated with temperate running water in the southern Andes; the extent of its populations is not established by the sources consulted.
sections.conservation: No species-level conservation category or population trend was established in the sources consulted.
